issues.issue: Did the Federal Court wrongly set aside the Board's finding that B010 received no material benefit from his work as a crew member?
issues.applicant_position: B010: the Board's finding of no material benefit should stand; the Federal Court wrongly substituted its own view of the evidence.
issues.result_quote: Respectfully, the Federal Court erred by substituting its assessment of the evidence for that of the Board.

issues.issue: What standard of review applies to the Board's interpretation of 'people smuggling' in paragraph 37(1)(b)?
issues.applicant_position: Appellants: correctness applies to inadmissibility interpretation, and the Federal Court wrongly applied reasonableness.
issues.respondent_position: Minister: also argues that correctness, not reasonableness, should apply to the Board's interpretation.
issues.result_quote: I conclude that the Federal Court correctly selected the reasonableness standard of review as the standard

issues.issue: Was the Board's conclusion that people smuggling requires no material benefit from the smuggler reasonable?
issues.applicant_position: Appellants: the Protocol definition requires a material benefit, and s.3(3)(f) requires compliance with it.
issues.result_quote: I see no error in his application of the standard of review or in his analysis.

issues.issue: Does defining people smuggling by s.117 breach Canada's Protocol or Refugee Convention non-refoulement obligations?
issues.applicant_position: Appellants: a no-benefit reading breaches Canada's non-refoulement obligations and curtails refugee protection.
issues.result_quote: a finding of inadmissibility is not the equivalent of removal or refoulement

issues.issue: Does a no-benefit reading produce absurd results that the court should avoid?
issues.applicant_position: Appellants: the no-benefit reading is absurd, for example making family members inadmissible for helping each other flee.
issues.respondent_position: Minister: the appellants' reading would itself be absurd, since a convicted smuggler could escape inadmissibility.
issues.result_quote: the alleged absurdity of an outcome can not defeat a clear statement of Parliamentary intent

issues.issue: Does the Attorney General consent requirement in s.117(4) show Parliament meant not all smuggling to be inadmissible (B010)?
issues.applicant_position: B010: the s.117(4) Attorney General consent shows not every smuggling case is intended to be caught; the Board ignored this.
issues.result_quote: These provisions provide sufficient flexibility to respond to special cases

issues.issue: Must a refugee claimant hold a visa or other document to enter Canada, so that the s.117 elements are met (B072)?
issues.applicant_position: B072: refugee claimants need not hold visas or documents to enter Canada, so the s.117 elements are not met.
issues.result_quote: I disagree that refugee claimants are not required to possess travel documents

issues.issue: Must a person be charged or arrested before being found inadmissible under paragraph 37(1)(b) (B072)?
issues.applicant_position: B072: inadmissibility under paragraph 37(1)(b) requires a charge or arrest for a transnational crime.
issues.result_quote: there is no requirement that a person be charged or arrested before a determination of inadmissibility may be made
